title: Goodram PX700 2TB SSD Review — High-end punch on a budget core
content: The Goodram PX700 matches good all-around performance with high power-efficiency in a cool-running package. It performs mostly like a premium drive, although pricing remains a concern.

title: Nvidia's unreleased RTX 3070 Ti 16GB comes to life thanks to a modder's crazy GDDR6 swap — Frankenstein card combines RTX 3070 PCB and new VRAM with RTX 3070 Ti GPU
content: A modder has recreated the never-released RTX 3070 Ti with 16GB of VRAM using GDDR6 chips instead of the GDDR6X the retail 3070 Ti actually shipped with.

title: Big Tech eyes glacier-strewn Patagonia for building mega AI data centers — region offers 17,300 glaciers, coldness, and cheap energy, but fiber lines are scarce
content: Patagonia, a region of Argentina with 17,300 glaciers has the potential to turn into a data center hotspot.

title: AI servers push Asus' August revenue up 51%
content: Asus reported consolidated revenue of NT$94.96 billion (US$3.02 billion) in August 2026, up 12.87% from July and 51.17% from a year earlier — the second-highest monthly figure in company history. Revenue for the first eight months reached NT$645.19 billion (US$20.5 billion), up 42.3% year over year. The company attributed the gain to AI server and PC demand, with motherboard orders also recovering.

title: OpenAI's deeper Samsung tie-up lands on a foundry that is running out of capacity
content: For Samsung Electronics' two loss-making logic businesses, OpenAI's declaration that it is jointly producing and researching next-generation chips with the Korean company matters less as a new logo on the customer list than as a sign of where Samsung's advanced wafers actually go.

title: AI computing power propels tech sector to US$30 trillion, putting servers at the core of 2027's supply chain
content: Taiwan's Market Intelligence & Consulting Institute (MIC) expects servers and data center supply chains to become the primary growth drivers for major information and communications technology (ICT) products in 2027. Global server shipments are projected to increase 12.4% year-over-year to 18.6 million units, with AI server shipments rising 17.8% to 5.4 million units.

title: Enterprise AI spending gives Taiwan's Systex a new growth wing
content: Systex reported consolidated revenue of NT$5.9 billion (approximately US$187 million) in August 2026, up 61.91% from NT$3.64 billion a year earlier. Revenue for the first eight months reached NT$38.01 billion, rising 39.65% from NT$27.22 billion in the same period of 2025. Both monthly and cumulative revenue hit record highs for their respective periods.

title: Huaqin signs Nanchang projects as robotics push widens
content: Huaqin Technology has signed two new projects in Nanchang High-tech Zone, expanding the smart-hardware ODM group's local manufacturing base into embodied-AI robotics and data collection, according to Hongguan News reporting on Sina Finance.

title: Jin Lian Cheng expands into semiconductor wafer fab UPS battery recycling
content: Jin Lian Cheng Resources completed an upgrade to its desulfurization production line as demand increased for lead-acid battery recycling tied to high-spec uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems used by semiconductor plants. The Taiwanese waste lead-acid battery processor said the upgrade restored normal operations while improving sulfur oxide treatment, real-time monitoring, and environmental management.

title: Cambricon wins PyTorch Foundation board seat in bid to strengthen China AI chip software ecosystem
content: Chinese AI chip developer Cambricon said on September 8 that it has formally joined the PyTorch Foundation as a platinum member, the organisation's highest membership tier, securing a seat on its governing board.

title: Google steps up green power purchases in Taiwan for 24/7 carbon-free electricity
content: Over the past half-year, multinational companies and semiconductor suppliers have pressed the government to reduce surplus power conditions. To increase the flexibility of green power transfer and matching, Taiwan Power (Taipower) has planned to launch Sandbox 3.0 in October 2026, which market watchers expect will help address TSMC's surplus electricity issue and add flexibility to Taiwan's renewable energy market.

title: Ledlink Optics posts 21-month revenue high on AI server, auto demand
content: Ledlink Optics reported that August revenue climbed on stronger AI server and automotive demand, with consolidated revenue reaching NT$134 million. The figure rose 3.21% from July and 20.42% from a year earlier, as the Taiwan-based supplier said both businesses supported growth heading into the second half of the year.

title: China expands OLED capacity, challenging South Korea in IT and automotive display markets
content: South Korea's long-standing dominance in the global display market is facing an aggressive challenge as major Chinese panel makers—including BOE, China Star Optoelectronics Technology (CSOT), and Visionox—rapidly expand their organic light-emitting diode (OLED) production capacity. title: Samsung turns to Japan for packaging edge, narrows HBM gap with SK Hynix
content: Samsung Electronics has opened an advanced packaging research center in Yokohama, bringing development work closer to Japanese suppliers that provide critical materials and equipment for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) as the company works to narrow its market-share gap with SK Hynix.

title: Getac sees growing drone orders, with 2027 revenue contribution reaching up to 12%
content: Getac Holdings is expanding aggressively into drone opportunities on the back of its strong industrial rugged computer foundation, making the segment a continued growth driver in the second half of 2026.

title: Realtek expands cloud AI push with ASIC and SSD chips
content: Realtek chairman Sun-Chien Chiu, who received an honorary fellowship from Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI) this week, said in a public interview that the company is already generating revenue from ASIC projects and has started expanding into 3nm products. Although Realtek's ASIC business is still far smaller than MediaTek's, Chiu said it will continue to grow as more projects come in.

title: Ample Electronic hits 120% utilization as MLCC customers step up copper paste orders
content: Ample Electronic Technology said strong demand for passive components and artificial intelligence (AI) server-related products is boosting business momentum, as multi-layer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) customers ramp up copper paste purchases.

title: Kioxia rules out deeper SK Hynix ties, resists further NAND price hikes
content: Kioxia has ruled out deeper manufacturing ties with SK Hynix while resisting another round of aggressive NAND price increases, leaning instead on longer customer contracts and disciplined capacity expansion as data-center demand keeps memory supply tight.

title: Update: US finalizes US$775 million in CHIPS quantum awards, with equity attached
content: Washington has converted the largest federal bet yet on quantum computing from a promise into a contract, and it is taking ownership in return. On Sept. 8, the US Department of Commerce announced the signing of final awards with five companies under the CHIPS and Science Act: up to US$375 million for GlobalFoundries and up to US$100 million each for Rigetti, D-Wave, PsiQuantum, and Quantinuum, according to five separate announcements posted by the National Institute of Standards and Technology.

title: Verizon, Corning strike multi-billion-dollar fiber deal for broadband and AI buildout
content: Verizon and Corning have agreed to a multi-billion-dollar supply deal that could shape broadband access and artificial intelligence infrastructure well beyond the US. The pact underscores how telecom networks are becoming a shared foundation for consumer internet, enterprise connectivity, and the data-heavy systems driving the next wave of AI services.

Samsung and SK hynix are at the heart of a historic shortage in the memory chip market as the demand from AI data centers continues to stress their production capacity. title: CXMT Faces HBM Memory Chip Shock As Yields Sink To 25% With Close To 80 Out Of 100 HBM3 Chips Failing Final Tests, Says Report
content: Chinese memory firm CXMT is facing yield problems with its HBM memory chip production, according to a report in the Korean media. HBM memory chips are significantly harder to manufacture than traditional DRAM modules due to assembly complications. CXMT's rise in the global memory market has been due to the firm's ability to supply DRAM modules as the major legacy memory manufacturers focus on HBM production.
